name: Sedma Dominoes
description: Connecting domino game named after the Czech word for seven. Four players receive seven tiles each; no boneyard. Lead rotates; the leader must set a double. Players in turn extend the train from one side only or pass. Points for setting doubles; game to 60.

overview.description: Connecting domino game named after the Czech word for seven. Four players receive seven tiles each; no boneyard. Lead rotates; the leader must set a double. Players in turn extend the train from one side only or pass. Points for setting doubles; game to 60.

history.origins: Sedma (Czech for seven) is a connecting domino game; the layout is built in one direction only and extra points are scored for playing doubles. Related in name to the Czech card game Sedma.
timeline: Rules first published in English in 2001.
history.cultural: Played in the Czech Republic; the name means 'seven' in Czech. Often played as a family or children's connecting game.
history.evolution: Sedma is a version of the children's game One-Armed Pete (One Arm Joe), related to the Chinese domino game Tsair Deng (slanted nails).

setup.players: Four players use a double-six domino set; each receives seven tiles. There is no boneyard; play is individual with no partnerships.
setup.dealing: Each player receives seven tiles. There is no boneyard.

rules.objective: Score points by setting doubles. When you set a double you score one point for it plus one point for each double already in the train that is lower than yours. First player or team to reach 60 points wins the game.
rules.gameplay: The lead rotates each round; the first round leader is chosen by chance. The player who is offered the lead must set a double; if they have no double, the lead passes left until someone can. Others build a train from one side only of the lead double; the first tile is played crosswise to mark the start. If you have a tile matching the open end you play it; otherwise you pass. The game ends when blocked or when one player dominoes.
keyRules: Double-6 set; four players; seven tiles each; no boneyard
Leader must set a double or pass lead left
Train builds from one side only of the lead double; first tile crosswise
Doubles order for scoring: 0-0 through 6-6, then 0-0 again (double blank is both high and low)

strategy.basic: Hold doubles to score when lower doubles are already in the train; try to play so you can set a double after others.
tips: The lead must set a double or pass left; if you have several doubles, leading when you can set a high one may score more.

scoring.description: When you set a double you score one point for it plus one for each double already in the train lower than yours. Double order: 0-0 through 6-6 then 0-0 again.
scoring.winCondition: First player or team to reach 60 points wins the game.

synthesis.shortDescription: Connecting domino game to 60 points; set doubles to score.
